devdoc.author: Non-Fungible Technologies, Inc. This contract is used to hold funds for the Arcade treasury. Each token held by this contract has three thresholds associated with it: (1) large amount, (2) medium amount, and (3) small amount. The only way to modify these thresholds is via the governance timelock which holds the ADMIN role. For each spend threshold, there is a corresponding spend function which can be called by only the CORE_VOTING_ROLE. In the Core Voting contract, a custom quorum for each spend function shall be set to the appropriate threshold. In order to enable the GSC to execute smaller spends from the Treasury without going through the entire governance process, the GSC has an allowance for each token. The GSC can spend up to the allowance amount for each token. The GSC allowance can be updated by the contract's ADMIN role. When updating the GSC's allowance for a specific token, the allowance cannot be higher than the small threshold set for the token. This is to force spends larger than the small threshold to always be voted on by governance. Additionally, there is a cool down period between each GSC allowance update of 7 days.

getRoleAdmin(bytes32).details: Returns the admin role that controls `role`. See {grantRole} and {revokeRole}. To change a role's admin, use {_setRoleAdmin}.

getRoleMember(bytes32,uint256).details: Returns one of the accounts that have `role`. `index` must be a value between 0 and {getRoleMemberCount}, non-inclusive. Role bearers are not sorted in any particular way, and their ordering may change at any point. WARNING: When using {getRoleMember} and {getRoleMemberCount}, make sure you perform all queries on the same block. See the following https://forum.openzeppelin.com/t/iterating-over-elements-on-enumerableset-in-openzeppelin-contracts/2296[forum post] for more information.

getRoleMemberCount(bytes32).details: Returns the number of accounts that have `role`. Can be used together with {getRoleMember} to enumerate all bearers of a role.

T_BlockSpendLimit().notice: Cannot withdraw or approve more than each tokens preset spend limits per block.

T_CoolDownPeriod(uint256,uint256).notice: Must wait 7 days since last allowance was set to set a new one.

T_InvalidAllowance(uint256,uint256).notice: When setting a new GSC allowance for a token it cannot be more than that tokens small spend threshold.

T_InvalidTarget(address).notice: Cannot make calls to addresses which have thresholds set. This is also a way to block calls to unwanted addresses or bypass treasury withdraw functions.

T_ThresholdsNotAscending().notice: Thresholds must be in ascending order.

T_ZeroAddress(string).notice: Zero address passed in where not allowed.

T_ZeroAmount().notice: Cannot pass zero as an amount.

GSCAllowanceUpdated(address,uint256).notice: event emitted when the GSC allowance is updated for a token

SpendThresholdsUpdated(address,(uint256,.notice: event emitted when a token's spend thresholds are updated

TreasuryApproval(address,address,uint256.notice: event emitted when a token amount is approved for spending

TreasuryTransfer(address,address,uint256.notice: event emitted when a token is spent

SET_ALLOWANCE_COOL_DOWN().notice: constant which represents the minimum amount of time between allowance sets

approveLargeSpend(address,address,uint25.notice: function to approve a large amount of tokens from the treasury. This function         should have the highest quorum of the three approve functions.

approveMediumSpend(address,address,uint2.notice: function to approve a medium amount of tokens from the treasury. This function         should have the middle quorum of the three approve functions.

approveSmallSpend(address,address,uint25.notice: function to approve a small amount of tokens from the treasury. This function         should have the lowest quorum of the three approve functions.

batchCalls(address[],bytes[]).notice: function to execute arbitrary calls from the treasury. This function is only         callable by the contract admin. All calls are executed in order, and if any of them fail         the entire transaction is reverted.

blockExpenditure(uint256,uint256).notice: mapping to track the amount spent in a block by threshold level, including approvals

gscAllowance(address).notice: mapping of token address to GSC allowance amount

gscApprove(address,address,uint256).notice: function for the GSC to approve tokens to be pulled from the treasury. The amount to         be approved must be less than or equal to the GSC's allowance for that specific token.

gscSpend(address,uint256,address).notice: function for the GSC to spend tokens from the treasury. The amount to be         spent must be less than or equal to the GSC's allowance for that specific token.

largeSpend(address,uint256,address).notice: function to spend a large amount of tokens from the treasury. This function         should have the highest quorum of the three spend functions.

lastAllowanceSet(address).notice: the last timestamp when the allowance was set for a token

mediumSpend(address,uint256,address).notice: function to spend a medium amount of tokens from the treasury. This function         should have the middle quorum of the three spend functions.

setGSCAllowance(address,uint256).notice: function to set the GSC allowance for a token. This function is only callable         by the contract admin. The new allowance must be less than or equal to the small         spend threshold for that specific token. There is a cool down period of 7 days         after this function has been called where it cannot be called again. Once the cooldown         period is over the allowance can be updated by the admin again.

setThreshold(address,(uint256,uint256,ui.notice: function to set the spend/approve thresholds for a token. This function is only         callable by the contract admin.

smallSpend(address,uint256,address).notice: function to spend a small amount of tokens from the treasury. This function         should have the lowest quorum of the three spend functions.

spendThresholds(address).notice: mapping of token address to spend thresholds
